easy-day-js npm postinstall dropper: node executing setup.cjs --no-warnings AIInstallation High
Hunts the install-time loader from the @mastra/easy-day-js supply-chain compromise, where the malicious dayjs look-alike's postinstall hook runs 'node setup.cjs --no-warnings', which disables TLS verification, pulls a second stage, spawns it detached and self-deletes. Article-specific because it keys on the exact dropper filename and flag invoked during npm install. Rationale: Keys on the exact dropper invocation 'node setup.cjs --no-warnings' documented by Microsoft Threat Intel and Socket for the easy-day-js loader — a combination that does not occur in normal npm installs. Cross-checked Microsoft + Socket writeups. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://socket.dev/blog/mastra-npm-packages-compromised • https://snyk.io/blog/a-forgotten-contributor-account-compromised-the-entire-mastra-npm-package-scope/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate internal npm package that ships a benign setup.cjs build script (rare, but possible on CI build agents)
  • Developer manually running 'node setup.cjs' for an unrelated project that happens to use that filename
  • CI/CD runner installing internal tooling whose postinstall uses a setup.cjs convention
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe") and FolderPath startswith "C:\\BuildAgent\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree for the node.exe hit — confirm parent is an npm/install context and look for a sibling detached node child spawning a randomly-named .js from %TEMP%. Check the working dir for node_modules/easy-day-js and grep package-lock for easy-day-js@1.11.22 (SHA256 221c45a7...badf). 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the detached node and any PowerShell children, and rotate any crypto-wallet/browser-stored credentials and npm/CI tokens used on that machine. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2/UC3/UC4 on the same DeviceId — C2 to 23.254.164.0/24, the NvmProtocal Run key, and protocal.cjs/NodePackages drops.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "setup.cjs" and ProcessCommandLine has "--no-warnings"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe"
| where CommandLine has "setup.cjs" and CommandLine has "--no-warnings"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

easy-day-js stealer C2 beacon to Hostwinds 23.254.164.0/24 (ports 8000/443) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound connections to the easy-day-js / Sapphire Sleet C2 infrastructure: payload fetch from 23.254.164.92:8000 and HTTPS exfiltration to 23.254.164.123:443, plus the named Hostwinds/onweblive domains. Article-specific because it uses the hardcoded second-source-confirmed C2 IPs and hostnames, not a generic egress pattern. Rationale: 23.254.164.92:8000 (payload) and 23.254.164.123:443 (exfil), plus onweblive/hostwindsdns domains, are hardcoded C2 IOCs confirmed independently by Socket and Microsoft — any internal host reaching them is high-fidelity compromise. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/mastra-npm-packages-compromised • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://safedep.io/mastra-npm-scope-takeover-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1571
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A different benign tenant happens to lease an adjacent Hostwinds IP in 23.254.164.0/24 after takedown (verify the exact /32s 23.254.164.92 and .123)
  • Security researcher / sandbox detonating the sample from a corporate range
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling actively probing the C2 for tracking
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is node.exe / powershell.exe (not a browser) and capture the exact remote IP+port — 23.254.164.92:8000 = stage-2 pull, 23.254.164.123:443 = data exfil. Note timestamp for scoping. 2) Contain: block 23.254.164.0/24 at the egress firewall, isolate the host, and treat any data sent to .123:443 as exfiltrated — force-rotate wallet seeds, browser-saved creds and tokens. 3) Hunt: sweep all hosts for the same /24, then pivot to UC1 (setup.cjs), UC3 (NvmProtocal), UC4 (protocal.cjs) to find the install root cause.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("teams.onweblive.org","maskasd.com","onweblive.org","hwsrv-1327786.hostwindsdns.com","hwsrv-1327785.hostwindsdns.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, DstDomain
| order by TimeGenerated desc

easy-day-js Windows persistence: Run key 'NvmProtocal' / protocal.cjs autostart AIInstallation High
Hunts the second-stage implant's Windows persistence — an HKCU Run value named 'NvmProtocal' (and the scdev service / com.nvm.protocal artifacts) launching protocal.cjs from a NodePackages directory. Article-specific because it pins on the malware's unique autostart value name and implant filename rather than generic Run-key writes. Rationale: The autostart value name 'NvmProtocal' and implant name 'protocal.cjs' (deliberate misspellings) plus the 'NodePackages' drop dir are unique implant strings confirmed by Microsoft and Socket — near-zero legitimate collision. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://socket.dev/blog/mastra-npm-packages-compromised
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate NVM (Node Version Manager) install writing a Run entry — but those use 'nvm'/'nvm-windows', not the misspelled 'NvmProtocal'
  • Sysadmin scripting a custom autostart that coincidentally references a NodePackages path
  • Security tooling restoring/quarantining the registry value (will show defender/AV as initiating process)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe") and RegistryValueData !has "\\nvm\\nvm.exe"
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the full RegistryValueData — it should point at protocal.cjs under a NodePackages dir; capture the InitiatingProcess (expect node.exe/powershell.exe). Check for the scdev service and C:\ProgramData\system.bat alongside it. 2) Contain: isolate host, delete the NvmProtocal value + scdev service + protocal.cjs implant, kill the running implant process. 3) Hunt: search org-wide for the same value name and for the cross-platform variants (com.nvm.protocal.plist on macOS, nvmconf.service on Linux) via UC4; trace back to the install via UC1.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where (RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run" and RegistryValueName =~ "NvmProtocal")
   or RegistryValueData has_any ("protocal.cjs","NodePackages","com.nvm.protocal")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run" and RegistryValue =~ "NvmProtocal")
   or RegistryValueData has_any ("protocal.cjs","NodePackages","com.nvm.protocal")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

easy-day-js implant artifacts dropped: protocal.cjs / NodePackages / cross-OS persistence files AIInstallation High
Hunts on-disk artifacts of the easy-day-js second stage across Windows, macOS and Linux: the implant 'protocal.cjs', the NodePackages drop directory, the loader marker files .pkg_history/.pkg_logs, and the OS-specific persistence units com.nvm.protocal.plist and nvmconf.service. Article-specific because every filename is a unique, second-source-confirmed implant artifact. Rationale: protocal.cjs, com.nvm.protocal.plist, nvmconf.service, NodePackages and the .pkg_history/.pkg_logs markers are unique implant/loader filenames confirmed by Microsoft and Socket — a file write of any is high-confidence compromise across Windows/macOS/Linux. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://socket.dev/blog/mastra-npm-packages-compromised • https://safedep.io/mastra-npm-scope-takeover-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1543.002 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A benign internal tool legitimately named 'NodePackages' as a directory (verify it isn't dropping protocal.cjs)
  • Backup/EDR quarantine software copying the artifacts into a vault path (initiating process will be the security tool)
  • A developer's own .plist/.service file that coincidentally matches — confirm the com.nvm.protocal / nvmconf naming exactly
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msmpeng.exe","sense.exe","backup.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the writing process is node.exe/powershell.exe and the file is the implant (hash protocal.cjs vs 50eae63d...edd65). Note which persistence unit was written to map the OS. 2) Contain: isolate the host, remove protocal.cjs and the persistence unit (Run key / plist / systemd), kill the detached implant, and revoke wallet + browser-stored credentials. 3) Hunt: org-wide sweep for these filenames and the NodePackages dir, then correlate to UC1 (setup.cjs install) and UC2 (C2 to 23.254.164.0/24) on the same hosts to bound the campaign.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("protocal.cjs","nvmconf.service","com.nvm.protocal.plist",".pkg_history",".pkg_logs")
   or FolderPath has "NodePackages"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName in~ ("protocal.cjs","nvmconf.service","com.nvm.protocal.plist",".pkg_history",".pkg_logs")
   or TargetFilePath has "NodePackages"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: |

    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "c38954e85bf5433e61e7c8f4230336695624ae88b6953afabf7bf817aa91b638", "cdec8b20338beb708b5be8d3d7a3041a35a8b0fb92f9186262f312d55ff82066", "9570f77a5e1511869f4e554e7166df9fde081f2583e293c2569621792ed7d9c9", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf") or SHA1 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "c38954e85bf5433e61e7c8f4230336695624ae88b6953afabf7bf817aa91b638", "cdec8b20338beb708b5be8d3d7a3041a35a8b0fb92f9186262f312d55ff82066", "9570f77a5e1511869f4e554e7166df9fde081f2583e293c2569621792ed7d9c9", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf") or MD5 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "c38954e85bf5433e61e7c8f4230336695624ae88b6953afabf7bf817aa91b638", "cdec8b20338beb708b5be8d3d7a3041a35a8b0fb92f9186262f312d55ff82066", "9570f77a5e1511869f4e554e7166df9fde081f2583e293c2569621792ed7d9c9", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "c38954e85bf5433e61e7c8f4230336695624ae88b6953afabf7bf817aa91b638", "cdec8b20338beb708b5be8d3d7a3041a35a8b0fb92f9186262f312d55ff82066", "9570f77a5e1511869f4e554e7166df9fde081f2583e293c2569621792ed7d9c9", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf") or SHA1 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "c38954e85bf5433e61e7c8f4230336695624ae88b6953afabf7bf817aa91b638", "cdec8b20338beb708b5be8d3d7a3041a35a8b0fb92f9186262f312d55ff82066", "9570f77a5e1511869f4e554e7166df9fde081f2583e293c2569621792ed7d9c9", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf") or MD5 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "c38954e85bf5433e61e7c8f4230336695624ae88b6953afabf7bf817aa91b638", "cdec8b20338beb708b5be8d3d7a3041a35a8b0fb92f9186262f312d55ff82066", "9570f77a5e1511869f4e554e7166df9fde081f2583e293c2569621792ed7d9c9", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "c38954e85bf5433e61e7c8f4230336695624ae88b6953afabf7bf817aa91b638", "cdec8b20338beb708b5be8d3d7a3041a35a8b0fb92f9186262f312d55ff82066", "9570f77a5e1511869f4e554e7166df9fde081f2583e293c2569621792ed7d9c9", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

NVD in the AI Era: The Case for Multi-Source Vulnerability Intelligence

Snyk
2026-06-25 1 use case 2 techniques 3 kill-chain phases detected

NIST’s shift to risk-based enrichment makes one thing clear: modern security teams need more than a single public source. In the AI era, trusted vulnerability intelligence depends on multiple signals, human validation, and clear context.

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-12569", "CVE-2026-4681")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-12569", "CVE-2026-4681")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c") or SHA1 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c") or MD5 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c") or SHA1 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c") or MD5 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Bun runtime executing codfish/semantic-release-action index.js payload on CI runner AIInstallation High
Hunts the Miasma composite-action payload step on a GitHub Actions runner: the bun runtime invoked as 'bun run $GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/index.js' where the action path resolves to codfish/semantic-release-action. The legitimate v1 action was Docker-based (entrypoint.js) and never used bun, so bun executing index.js from this action's path is the compromise itself. Rationale: Anchors on bun + 'index.js' + 'semantic-release-action' from the article's verbatim composite-action step ('bun run $GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/index.js'); GITHUB_ACTION_PATH expands to the _actions/codfish/semantic-release-action path so both tokens co-occur in the cmdline. The original Docker action never used bun, making this combination malicious by construction. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-github-action-codfish-steals-secrets • https://x.com/step_security/status/2069831503471882383 • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer locally testing bun against a project that happens to have a file named index.js inside a directory named semantic-release-action
  • An internal fork/mirror of the action legitimately re-tooled to use bun for builds
  • Security researchers detonating the IOC in a sandboxed CI runner
  • A monorepo with an unrelated package literally named 'semantic-release-action' built with bun
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full ProcessCommandLine and parent chain — confirm parent is a GitHub Actions runner (Runner.Worker/bash) and the action path resolves to codfish/semantic-release-action; capture the runner host and the repo/workflow that triggered it. 2) Contain: cancel/disable the affected workflow, rotate every secret that workflow could touch (GITHUB_TOKEN is auto-scoped but rotate any NPM_TOKEN / PAT / cloud creds), and pin the action to a known-clean SHA (v1.0.0–v1.10.0 or v2.0.0). 3) Hunt: search all repos for references to codfish/semantic-release-action@v2–v5, look for the index.js SHA256 (UC2) and bun→api.github.com egress (UC3) on the same runner, and review npm publish logs for unauthorized releases.

| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "semantic-release-action"

Known Miasma index.js payload hash present on CI runner (codfish action) AIDelivery High
Definitive IOC sweep for the byte-identical malicious index.js payload (sha256 9f93d77d...) dropped by the compromised codfish/semantic-release-action across DeviceFileEvents, DeviceProcessEvents and DeviceImageLoadEvents. Any host carrying this hash has pulled the trojanised action. Rationale: Uses the article's confirmed payload IOC (sha256 9f93d77d32833a515bc406c46da477142bb1ac2babeecb6aa42f98669a6db015, byte-identical across both malicious commits). A hash match is unambiguous, hence alerting. Sigma/Splunk/Datadog/Falcon left empty because file-write events on those stacks (Sysmon EID 11, CIM Endpoint.Filesystem, Falcon FileWritten) do not carry a SHA256 for a non-executed script file — the hash IOC only lives cleanly in Defender/ASIM file telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-github-action-codfish-steals-secrets • https://snyk.io/blog/miasma-supply-chain-attack-malicious-code-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages/
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.007
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A threat-intel analyst intentionally storing the IOC sample on a workstation for analysis
  • An AV/EDR quarantine copy of the file retaining the original hash
  • A sandbox/detonation host where the sample was deliberately staged
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the host is a CI runner and identify which workflow/repo pulled it; the InitiatingProcess shows whether bun executed it. 2) Contain: isolate the runner, kill the bun process tree, and rotate all secrets exposed to any workflow that ran on that runner (GITHUB_TOKEN scope, NPM_TOKEN with publish rights, cloud/CI PATs). 3) Hunt: enumerate every repo referencing codfish/semantic-release-action@v2/v2.2.1/v3*/v4*/v5*, repin to clean v1.x or v2.0.0, and check npm/registry audit logs for unexpected package publishes.
union DeviceFileEvents, DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 == "9f93d77d32833a515bc406c46da477142bb1ac2babeecb6aa42f98669a6db015"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA256 =~ "9f93d77d32833a515bc406c46da477142bb1ac2babeecb6aa42f98669a6db015"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
Bun process reaching GitHub commit-search API — Miasma dead-drop C2 AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the Miasma infrastructure-less C2: the bun-run payload polls GitHub's public commit-search API (api.github.com) for marker-tagged commits whose body it passes to eval(). Outbound to GitHub initiated specifically by the bun runtime (the 'Cleanup Action' step) is the dead-drop resolver beacon, distinct from normal git/node CI traffic. Rationale: Anchors on the article's described C2 design (Miasma polls GitHub's public commit-search API and eval()s the matching commit body) plus the bun-run payload step; corroborated by The Register/SafeDep on the leaked toolkit. Scoping egress to bun (not git/node/curl) and the action cmdline separates the dead-drop beacon from normal CI traffic to GitHub. Sentinel left empty because no process-attributed egress table is available in this tenant (ASIM ImNetworkSession/ImWebSession lack initiating-process), so the bun-specific pivot needs Defender DeviceNetworkEvents. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-github-action-codfish-steals-secrets • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/06/09/miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit-goes-public-on-github/5253074 • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate bun-based CI step that genuinely calls the GitHub API (e.g. bun-native release tooling fetching releases)
  • A self-hosted runner where bun is the standard JS runtime and hits api.github.com for package metadata
  • DNS telemetry attributing the resolution to bun when a child git subprocess actually made the call
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "semantic-release-action"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the bun process that made the request was launched from the codfish/semantic-release-action path (correlate with UC1) and pull the resolved IP plus any url query if captured. 2) Contain: isolate the runner, block egress from runner subnets to api.github.com for non-allowlisted processes, and rotate secrets exposed to workflows on that runner. 3) Hunt: capture the bun process memory/handles for evidence of Runner.Worker access (secret theft), look for the index.js hash (UC2) on the host, and review GitHub commit-search-API access patterns from other runners for the same dead-drop behaviour.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has "github.com"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "index.js" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "semantic-release-action"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has "github.com"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "index.js" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "semantic-release-action"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Bun Runtime DNS Query to GitHub API (Miasma Dead-Drop C2)
id: b8e1d57c-3a92-4c0e-9f6d-71a4e2c8b903
description: Detects the bun runtime resolving github.com, consistent with the Miasma payload polling the GitHub commit-search API as an infrastructure-less dead-drop resolver.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-github-action-codfish-steals-secrets
  - https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/06/09/miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit-goes-public-on-github/5253074
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/25
tags:
  - attack.t1102.001
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '/bun'
    QueryName|contains: 'github.com'
  condition: selection
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\bun.exe OR */bun OR *\BUN.EXE) @DestinationHostname:*github.com*
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/github\.com$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/\/bun(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.process_name="bun" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe") (All_Traffic.dest="*github.com*" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*github.com*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.process_name="bun" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe") (All_Traffic.dest="*github.com*" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*github.com*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"

      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f93d77d32833a515bc406c46da477142bb1ac2babeecb6aa42f98669a6db015", "5792aba0e2180b9b80b77644370a6889d5817456", "bcb6b1d409144318e8fad2171d6fe06d02299d1a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f93d77d32833a515bc406c46da477142bb1ac2babeecb6aa42f98669a6db015", "5792aba0e2180b9b80b77644370a6889d5817456", "bcb6b1d409144318e8fad2171d6fe06d02299d1a") or MD5 in~ ("9f93d77d32833a515bc406c46da477142bb1ac2babeecb6aa42f98669a6db015", "5792aba0e2180b9b80b77644370a6889d5817456", "bcb6b1d409144318e8fad2171d6fe06d02299d1a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f93d77d32833a515bc406c46da477142bb1ac2babeecb6aa42f98669a6db015", "5792aba0e2180b9b80b77644370a6889d5817456", "bcb6b1d409144318e8fad2171d6fe06d02299d1a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f93d77d32833a515bc406c46da477142bb1ac2babeecb6aa42f98669a6db015", "5792aba0e2180b9b80b77644370a6889d5817456", "bcb6b1d409144318e8fad2171d6fe06d02299d1a") or MD5 in~ ("9f93d77d32833a515bc406c46da477142bb1ac2babeecb6aa42f98669a6db015", "5792aba0e2180b9b80b77644370a6889d5817456", "bcb6b1d409144318e8fad2171d6fe06d02299d1a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f93d77d32833a515bc406c46da477142bb1ac2babeecb6aa42f98669a6db015", "5792aba0e2180b9b80b77644370a6889d5817456", "bcb6b1d409144318e8fad2171d6fe06d02299d1a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — ESET takes part in Operation Endgame to disrupt Amadey and Stealc
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",

                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] macOS.Gaslight Telegram Bot API C2 polling from non-browser process · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] macOS.Gaslight keychain theft + collected_data.zip staging · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
macOS.Gaslight Telegram Bot API C2 polling from non-browser process AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts macOS endpoints resolving/connecting to api.telegram.org from a process that is not a known browser or the legitimate Telegram desktop client. macOS.Gaslight runs its C2 as a Telegram Bot API getUpdates polling loop, so sustained api.telegram.org traffic from an ad-hoc-signed Rust binary is the C2 fingerprint. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim getUpdates Telegram Bot API C2 (code block 2) plus the api.telegram.org endpoint; non-browser/non-Telegram initiating process is the differentiator. Cross-checked against SentinelLABS, Infosecurity Magazine and the PXA/Ghost-in-the-Zip Telegram-C2 reporting. Cross-checked against: • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/macos-gaslight-rust-backdoor/ • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/ghost-in-the-zip-new-pxa-stealer-and-its-telegram-powered-ecosystem/
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Telegram Desktop client installed under a non-standard process name
  • Developer/CI tooling using a Telegram bot for build notifications
  • Marketing or alerting scripts (python/node) posting to a Telegram bot
  • Browser extensions or Electron apps embedding Telegram web
  • Security tooling that itself proxies Telegram traffic
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/Applications/Telegram.app"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName/SHA256 and folder path; confirm it is not Telegram Desktop or a sanctioned bot integration, and check if the binary is ad-hoc signed in an unusual path (e.g. user temp/Application Support). 2) Contain: isolate the host in MDE/Falcon, kill the polling process, and block the resolved IPs at egress. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same SHA256/parent across the fleet, and look for login.keychain-db copies, collected_data.zip, and the com.apple.system.services.activity LaunchAgent on the same host.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has "api.telegram.org"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("Telegram","Telegram.app","Safari","com.apple.Safari","Google Chrome","Google Chrome Helper","firefox","Brave Browser","com.apple.WebKit.Networking","nsurlsessiond")
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), DistinctMinutes=dcount(bin(Timestamp,1m)) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteUrl
| order by LastSeen desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DnsQuery has "api.telegram.org"
| summarize Lookups=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery
| order by LastSeen desc

macOS.Gaslight keychain theft + collected_data.zip staging AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the macOS.Gaslight Python stealer copying login.keychain-db and archiving harvested data to collected_data.zip prior to Telegram exfiltration. The collected_data.zip filename and a login.keychain-db copy by a non-Apple process are high-fidelity collection indicators. Rationale: Uses the article's exact collection artifacts: a raw copy of login.keychain-db and the temp/collected_data.zip archive. SentinelLABS notes AMOS/early Rust macOS stealers harvest the same login.keychain-db, and Jamf documents DumpKeychain()-style theft, so the zip filename is the novel high-fidelity anchor. Cross-checked against: • https://www.jamf.com/blog/pyinstaller-malware-jamf-threat-labs/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/02/02/infostealers-without-borders-macos-python-stealers-and-platform-abuse/
ATT&CKT1555.001 T1560.001 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Time Machine / backupd legitimately reading login.keychain-db
  • Keychain First Aid or migration assistant copying the keychain during OS upgrade
  • Admin manually backing up ~/Library/Keychains before re-imaging
  • A user-created archive coincidentally named collected_data.zip (rare)
  • MDM agents snapshotting user profiles
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName =~ "login.keychain-db" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("backupd","securityd","Migration Assistant"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess copying login.keychain-db / writing collected_data.zip — legitimate copies come from backupd/securityd, not a user-temp binary. 2) Contain: isolate host, kill the process, and force-rotate any credentials/secrets stored in that user's keychain (SSO, VPN, cloud, SSH passphrases). 3) Hunt: look for the collected_data.zip being uploaded to api.telegram.org, the com.apple.system.services.activity LaunchAgent, and the same parent binary's SHA256 elsewhere.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (FileName =~ "collected_data.zip")
    or (FileName =~ "login.keychain-db" and ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("backupd","mds","mds_stores","securityd","TimeMachine","cfprefsd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where (TargetFileName =~ "collected_data.zip")
    or (TargetFileName =~ "login.keychain-db" and EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed"))
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("backupd","mds","mds_stores","securityd","cfprefsd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

macOS.Gaslight LaunchAgent persistence masquerading as com.apple.system.services.activity AIInstallation High
Detects creation of a LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plist using the macOS.Gaslight persistence label com.apple.system.services.activity, an Apple-lookalike name not used by any genuine Apple service. Catches the implant establishing a persistent foothold. Rationale: Anchored on the exact LaunchAgent Label IOC from Table 2 (com.apple.system.services.activity) — there is no genuine Apple LaunchAgent by that name, so any plist bearing it is the implant. Consistent with SentinelLABS BlueNoroff/RustBucket macOS LaunchAgent persistence tradecraft. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/bluenoroff-hidden-risk-threat-actor-targets-macs-with-fake-crypto-news-and-novel-persistence/
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Apple LaunchAgents (com.apple.*) — but none use the exact services.activity suffix
  • Internal MDM/config-profile deployment pushing a custom-labeled agent (would not impersonate com.apple.*)
  • Security product creating its own LaunchDaemon under a vendor label
  • Developer testing a self-named LaunchAgent during app packaging
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the plist contents (ProgramArguments) and the InitiatingProcess that wrote it; confirm the referenced binary path and signing status. 2) Contain: unload the agent (launchctl bootout), quarantine the referenced binary, isolate the host. 3) Hunt: pivot to the binary's SHA256 across the fleet and check for api.telegram.org C2, login.keychain-db copies, and IOPMAssertionCreateWithName no-sleep behavior on the same host.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/" or FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchDaemons/"
| where FileName has "com.apple.system.services.activity"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/" or TargetFilePath has "/Library/LaunchDaemons/"
| where TargetFileName has "com.apple.system.services.activity"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

macOS.Gaslight self-staged standalone CPython 3.10.18 fetch (astral-sh python-build-standalone) AIInstallation High
Detects the macOS.Gaslight bash installer fetching a self-contained cpython-3.10.18 (build 20250708) interpreter from astral-sh/python-build-standalone at runtime — a novel staging step that precedes the Python keychain stealer. Anchors on the literal PY_VERSION/BUILD_DATE constants and the project name in the command line. Rationale: Uses the verbatim installer constants PY_VERSION=3.10.18 and BUILD_DATE=20250708 plus the astral-sh/python-build-standalone project name. SentinelLABS and Microsoft both flag runtime CPython staging as a novel macOS stealer delivery, making these literals high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/02/02/infostealers-without-borders-macos-python-stealers-and-platform-abuse/
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.004 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate developer using uv/rye/astral tooling that downloads python-build-standalone
  • CI runner provisioning a standalone CPython for build reproducibility
  • Data-science user manually fetching a portable CPython 3.10.18
  • Package manager (e.g. uv) auto-installing the same interpreter version
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("uv","rye","pyenv","brew")
Response runbook
1) Triage: examine the full command line and parent process — a developer fetch comes from uv/rye/terminal; the implant fetch is spawned by a base64-decoded bash installer with emoji/AI-comment tells. 2) Contain: if the parent is not a sanctioned dev tool, isolate host, kill the bash/curl chain, quarantine the staged interpreter dir. 3) Hunt: look for the subsequent Python process touching login.keychain-db, system_profiler, ps aux, and creating collected_data.zip, plus api.telegram.org egress.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "python-build-standalone"
    or (ProcessCommandLine has "astral-sh" and ProcessCommandLine has "cpython-3.10.18")
    or (ProcessCommandLine has "PY_VERSION=3.10.18" and ProcessCommandLine has "BUILD_DATE=20250708")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "python-build-standalone"
    or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "astral-sh" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "cpython-3.10.18")
    or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "PY_VERSION=3.10.18" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "BUILD_DATE=20250708")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

macOS.Gaslight known-bad file hashes (Mach-O implant, BONZAI sibling, Python/bash stages) AIInstallation Medium
Direct IOC sweep for the four published macOS.Gaslight SHA256 hashes and the ad-hoc signing SHA1, covering the Rust Mach-O implant, the sibling BONZAI sample, the base64 Python stealer, and the bash CPython installer. Fires on execution or file write of any known artifact. Rationale: Direct sweep on the four article SHA256 IOCs (Table 2) plus the ad-hoc signing SHA1 5555494492fc..., covering all four stage artifacts. Hash-only detections are deterministic; XProtect tracks the same sample by hash under MACOS_BONZAI_COBUCH. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/macos-gaslight-rust-backdoor-turns-prompt-injection-on-the-analyst-not-the-sandbox/ • https://cyberpress.org/gaslight-backdoor-misleads-analysts/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Hash collision is cryptographically implausible — effectively zero benign matches
  • Security researcher detonating the sample in a sanctioned analysis VM
  • Threat-intel platform re-scanning the artifact during enrichment
  • EDR's own quarantine/restore re-touching the file (Evidence=File)
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the matched hash and host; any non-sandbox match is a confirmed compromise — record device, user, folder path. 2) Contain: isolate host immediately, quarantine the file, and revoke credentials/keychain secrets for the logged-on user. 3) Hunt: pivot to api.telegram.org C2, the com.apple.system.services.activity LaunchAgent, login.keychain-db copies, and collected_data.zip; sweep the fleet for all four hashes and the ad-hoc signing identifier endpoint-macos-aarch64.
let GaslightHashes = dynamic(["6328567511d88fdc2ae0939c5ef17b7a63d2a833881900de018a4f12f4982525","77b4fd46994992f0e57302cfe76ed23c0d90101381d2b89fc2ddf5c4536e77ca","baabf249c77bc54c54ab0e66e15af798bd28aa5b4683554456a8b73ab8741239","b3c56d689414343589f38394d19ba2fe9a518133281200faa0556ba4e4136394"]);
let GaslightSha1 = "5555494492fc075f441637fb9d894913dde3a2ea";
union
( DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where SHA256 in~ (GaslightHashes) or SHA1 =~ GaslightSha1 | extend Evidence="Process" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Evidence, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine ),
( DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where SHA256 in~ (GaslightHashes) or SHA1 =~ GaslightSha1 | extend Evidence="File", ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Evidence, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine )
| order by Timestamp desc
let GaslightHashes = dynamic(["6328567511d88fdc2ae0939c5ef17b7a63d2a833881900de018a4f12f4982525","77b4fd46994992f0e57302cfe76ed23c0d90101381d2b89fc2ddf5c4536e77ca","baabf249c77bc54c54ab0e66e15af798bd28aa5b4683554456a8b73ab8741239","b3c56d689414343589f38394d19ba2fe9a518133281200faa0556ba4e4136394"]);
union
( ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where SHA256 in~ (GaslightHashes) | extend Evidence="Process" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, Evidence, TargetProcessName, SHA256, TargetProcessCommandLine ),
( ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (GaslightHashes) | extend Evidence="File", SHA256=TargetFileSHA256, TargetProcessName=ActingProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, Evidence, TargetProcessName, SHA256, TargetProcessCommandLine )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:

Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6328567511d88fdc2ae0939c5ef17b7a63d2a833881900de018a4f12f4982525", "77b4fd46994992f0e57302cfe76ed23c0d90101381d2b89fc2ddf5c4536e77ca", "baabf249c77bc54c54ab0e66e15af798bd28aa5b4683554456a8b73ab8741239", "b3c56d689414343589f38394d19ba2fe9a518133281200faa0556ba4e4136394") or SHA1 in~ ("6328567511d88fdc2ae0939c5ef17b7a63d2a833881900de018a4f12f4982525", "77b4fd46994992f0e57302cfe76ed23c0d90101381d2b89fc2ddf5c4536e77ca", "baabf249c77bc54c54ab0e66e15af798bd28aa5b4683554456a8b73ab8741239", "b3c56d689414343589f38394d19ba2fe9a518133281200faa0556ba4e4136394") or MD5 in~ ("6328567511d88fdc2ae0939c5ef17b7a63d2a833881900de018a4f12f4982525", "77b4fd46994992f0e57302cfe76ed23c0d90101381d2b89fc2ddf5c4536e77ca", "baabf249c77bc54c54ab0e66e15af798bd28aa5b4683554456a8b73ab8741239", "b3c56d689414343589f38394d19ba2fe9a518133281200faa0556ba4e4136394")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6328567511d88fdc2ae0939c5ef17b7a63d2a833881900de018a4f12f4982525", "77b4fd46994992f0e57302cfe76ed23c0d90101381d2b89fc2ddf5c4536e77ca", "baabf249c77bc54c54ab0e66e15af798bd28aa5b4683554456a8b73ab8741239", "b3c56d689414343589f38394d19ba2fe9a518133281200faa0556ba4e4136394") or SHA1 in~ ("6328567511d88fdc2ae0939c5ef17b7a63d2a833881900de018a4f12f4982525", "77b4fd46994992f0e57302cfe76ed23c0d90101381d2b89fc2ddf5c4536e77ca", "baabf249c77bc54c54ab0e66e15af798bd28aa5b4683554456a8b73ab8741239", "b3c56d689414343589f38394d19ba2fe9a518133281200faa0556ba4e4136394") or MD5 in~ ("6328567511d88fdc2ae0939c5ef17b7a63d2a833881900de018a4f12f4982525", "77b4fd46994992f0e57302cfe76ed23c0d90101381d2b89fc2ddf5c4536e77ca", "baabf249c77bc54c54ab0e66e15af798bd28aa5b4683554456a8b73ab8741239", "b3c56d689414343589f38394d19ba2fe9a518133281200faa0556ba4e4136394")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6328567511d88fdc2ae0939c5ef17b7a63d2a833881900de018a4f12f4982525", "77b4fd46994992f0e57302cfe76ed23c0d90101381d2b89fc2ddf5c4536e77ca", "baabf249c77bc54c54ab0e66e15af798bd28aa5b4683554456a8b73ab8741239", "b3c56d689414343589f38394d19ba2fe9a518133281200faa0556ba4e4136394"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
